$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: the matrix carries two sections the summary never counted. AC-11 is
a criterion the epic does not state, and a second AC-3 section contradicts the first with PARTIAL. Both
are named under mustNotReport, both have a threshold of 0, and readMatrix once discarded the first
before it could be counted, which is the defect the CHANGELOG records under maxInventedCriteria. This
case pins that both reach scoreRun, that the first AC-3 section keeps the floor, and that a citation
under either extra section is attributed to nobody.
The summary is seeded-correct-run's on purpose. A run that had counted AC-11 into its inventory would
also fail arithmetic, and that would blur what this case is about, which is the matrix alone.
derivation: The AC-11 heading shares the AC prefix with the oracle's ids and names no criterion in it, so readMatrix
records it as invented and opens no section for it; the export-manifest.spec.ts:20 line beneath it is
attributed to nothing. The second AC-3 heading names an id already seen, so it is recorded as a
duplicate and its PARTIAL and its citation are ignored; AC-3 stays FULL from the first section.
Statuses, gate, citations and every summary check are therefore seeded-correct-run's: 10 citations
resolve, and invented is ["AC-11"] and duplicates is ["AC-3"]. The set is not the clean one, so
